clusters.label: Temperature
clusters.definition: Physical quantity describing thermal state, used as a condition or variable in the supplied experiments and calculations.
clusters.reason: All denote the same thermal-state variable. Materials, measured or predicted responses, dependence directions, and conditions remain claim-specific. Debye temperature and temperature differences mentioned in context are not the referents of these nodes.

clusters.label: Ion thermodiffusion
clusters.reason: Both explicitly denote thermodiffusion of ions; the ion provider and subsequent electric-field-driven electronic transport describe its context and consequences.

clusters.label: High ionic thermovoltage
clusters.definition: A qualitatively high thermally generated voltage associated with ionic redistribution.
clusters.reason: Both describe high ionic thermovoltage in ionic thermoelectric gels. The ionogel evidence explicitly attributes it to the Soret effect; differing hosts and roles do not change the voltage concept or establish equal magnitudes.

clusters.label: Stretchability
clusters.definition: Mechanical ability of a material or device to undergo tensile extension without losing integrity.
clusters.reason: All explicitly describe the ability to stretch. Different materials, enabling structures, device contexts, and cycling conditions qualify individual claims; self-healing and bendability remain separate properties.
